hints: Take natural logarithms to linearise the exponential relationship in the plotted variables.
Rearrange into $y=m\ln x+c$ and read off the exact coefficient of $\ln x$.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of the given relationship $x = A(3^{-y})$:
$$\ln x = \ln\left(A(3^{-y})\right) = \ln A + \ln(3^{-y})$$

Apply the logarithm power law $\ln(3^{-y}) = -y\ln 3$:
$$\ln x = \ln A - y\ln 3$$

Rearrange the equation into explicit linear form $y = mX + c$, where $X = \ln x$:
$$y\ln 3 = \ln A - \ln x$$
$$y = -\dfrac{1}{\ln 3}\ln x + \dfrac{\ln A}{\ln 3}$$

Explain why the graph is a straight line:
Since this equation is linear in $y$ and $\ln x$ (of the form $y = mX + c$ where $m$ and $c$ are constants), plotting $y$ against $\ln x$ produces a straight line.

State the exact value of the gradient:
$$m = -\dfrac{1}{\ln 3}$$

hints: Use the intercept condition in the straight-line equation from part (a).
At the $y$-axis of a plot against $\ln x$, set $\ln x=0$ and $y=1.3$; do not set $x=0$.
Solve $\ln A=1.3\ln3$, exponentiate, and round $A$ only at the end.
walkthrough:
Identify the coordinates of the intercept on the $y$-axis:
On the graph of $y$ against $\ln x$, the vertical axis corresponds to $\ln x = 0$. The given intercept is $y = 1.3$.

Substitute $\ln x = 0$ and $y = 1.3$ into the linear equation $\ln x = \ln A - y\ln 3$:
$$0 = \ln A - 1.3\ln 3$$
$$\ln A = 1.3\ln 3$$

Apply the logarithm power rule:
$$\ln A = \ln(3^{1.3})$$

Exponentiate both sides to solve for $A$:
$$A = 3^{1.3}$$

Calculate $A$ numerically and round to 2 decimal places:
$$A \approx 4.171167 \dots \approx 4.17$$
